topic: MITRE ATT&CK Framework: Why It's Your Intelligence Compass, Not Your Checklist
post_text:
Most security teams treat MITRE ATT&CK like a shopping list to check off.

That's backwards.

Here's the real value: Imagine you're a detective investigating a crime scene. The evidence tells a story—broken window, missing jewelry, muddy footprints. You don't just catalog what happened. You map it against known criminal patterns to identify WHO did it and HOW.

That's MITRE ATT&CK.

It's a *library of adversary behaviors*, not a compliance requirement. When your SOC detects suspicious activity, ATT&CK helps you:

✓ Understand the attacker's objective (not just the tactic)
✓ Predict what comes next in their playbook
✓ Compare your incident to thousands of real-world campaigns
✓ Make smarter resource decisions about what to defend first

The framework has 14 tactics (reconnaissance, initial access, execution, etc.) and 700+ techniques—but you don't need to defend against all of them equally.

Your threat intel should drive your defensive strategy, not the other way around.

If adversaries targeting your industry favor data exfiltration via DNS tunneling, you hunt DNS anomalies. If they pivot through unpatched software, you patch ruthlessly.

MITRE ATT&CK is the *translation layer* between intelligence and defense.

Use it like a detective uses case files—to see patterns, not to build walls everywhere.

♻️ Repost if this helped someone.
